title: Keep a test set aside
summary: Training examples help choose a model. Test examples are kept aside to check it later. Keeping them separate helps reveal mistakes on unseen data.
introduction: Training examples help choose a model. Test examples are kept aside to check it later. Keeping them separate helps reveal mistakes on unseen data. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain keep a test set aside
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.code:
rows = [(1, 2), (2, 4), (3, 6), (4, 8)]
train = rows[:3]
test = rows[3:]
print(len(train), len(test))
blocks.title: Keep a test set aside

blocks.text: The output is 3 1. The first three pairs form the training list. The final pair forms the test list. This ordered split is only a small demonstration.

blocks.text: Real splits must account for time and related records; a simple slice is not always fair.
